chapter: Learning the drums and first job
title: Tom-toms, woodblock and details of Cottrell's lessons
summary: He used a Chinese tom-tom and woodblock, and recalls Cottrell's kindness, the practice pad, 50-cent lessons, and hearing him in brass bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah, I used a little tom-tom. Uh-huh.

What kind was that like? The Chinese... A little, uh, Chinese tom-tom. Chinese tom-tom. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Also, uh, woodblock. Did you mention if you had any woodblock? Yeah. I played a woodblock too. Is there anything else you can tell us about, uh, Cartrell, Louis Cartrell, how he played or what style? Oh, I know he was a very good drummer.

I can tell you he was a very good drummer. And I was interested in what he showed me, you know, what he taught me. And he's a very nice fella to get along with, cause nice disposition, you know. When I'd go to his house, he would greet me with a smile. Yeah.
Where did he live about then?
He lived down in it between, uh, Durbin and Roomba. Uh-huh. That's why he was here.
And you went to his house then for lessons? I went to his house, yeah.
Twice a week.
When you went there, did you take your drums with Durbin? He had a pad. He had a pad. We're gonna pad.
I just had to take the sticks, the little pad made out of skins, stuffed with cotton or something like that.
Do you remember anything, I know it's hard to remember all the way back when you started, but what kind of sticks did he advise you to have? Heavy sticks or light sticks or anything?
No, this was light, it was A1 I think it was. A1. Uh-huh. It was A1 I think.
Yeah.
I can't remember that good.
So you worked mostly just on the drum pad then, the snare sticks. Yeah, when he was teaching me. How often did you go for lessons, about once a week? Twice a week a week. Twice a week.
It was just 50 cents a lesson.
About how long were the lessons?
About a half hour, four or five minutes.
He was interested in teaching.
Yeah. Because my dad was good friends with him, you know.
If that bird bothers you, we can put him in the other room.
Oh yeah. That's okay.
He must like it, he's on your shoulder. Can you tell me anything about the brass bands, if you ever heard Louis Contrall and the brass bands?
Well yeah, I've heard them with Paris.
Paris. Which did he play, bass drum or snare drum? He played snare drum. Snare drum.
Yeah.
